rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says documentation is recommended, not obligatory, because a person may freely relinquish the right.
rows.anchor: الصحيح عدم الوجوب لأن للمرء أن يهب هذا الحق ويتركه بإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s inference is unsound: securing evidence is a different situation from voluntarily giving away a right.
rows.anchor: ولكنه مردود بأن مقام التوثق غير مقام التبرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law alerts right-holders against careless neglect and later regret, preserves trust between parties, eases a debtor’s resentment at documentation, and prevents disputes.
rows.anchor: ومقصد الشريعة تنبيه أصحاب الحقوق حتى لا يتساهلوا ثم يندموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing may be done by both contracting parties, or by one who gives the document to the other, when both can write; one party’s illiteracy undermines trust in the other’s handwriting.
rows.anchor: حالة كتابة المتداينين بخطيهما أو خط أحدهما ويسلمه للآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If either party cannot write, a third party writes their agreement, two witnesses attest it, and the document goes to the creditor; this was the common Arab situation because literacy was scarce and localized.
rows.anchor: حالة كتابة ثالث يتوسط بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At revelation, illiteracy was widespread among Arabs; writing was found in a few places and among only a small number in Mecca and Medina.
rows.anchor: وإنما كانت الكتابة في الأنبار والحيرة وبعض جهات اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative to have a writer between the parties addresses the contracting parties, since most were unable to write; its surface direction to the writer is rhetorical emphasis on their arranging documentation.
rows.anchor: أمر للمتداينين بأن يوسطوا كاتبا يكتب بينهم لأن غالب حالهم جهل الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request’s grammatical complement is the phrase between you, not the writer; the writer’s own commands are the prohibition on refusing and the following imperative to write.
rows.anchor: متعلق فعل الطلب هو ظرف بينكم وليس هذا أمرا للكاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-ʿadl means the right or truth, not the moral probity required of a witness, because the preposition bi rules out that sense.
rows.anchor: ليس العدل هنا بمعنى العدالة التي يوصف بها الشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes restrict the initial command to writing by a third-party scribe because that was usual and the next clause explains how to do it; the parties’ own writing is understood implicitly.
rows.anchor: على أن يكتبه كاتب غير المتداينين لأنه الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports the majority’s acceptance of written handwriting as evidence, since commissioning a scribe only helps if his handwriting can later be read.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كانت الآية حجة عند جمهور العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on a scribe refusing a request is a separate rule directed to the scribe, not a repetition of the command directed to the contracting parties.
rows.anchor: نهي لمن تطلب منه الكتابة بين المتداينين عن الامتناع منها إذا دعي إليها

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ, Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Ṭabarī hold that the ban is prohibitive, making acceptance an individual duty; the author endorses this as the sound view.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الربيع ومجاهد وعطاء والطبري

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan makes the duty individual only when there is one scribe locally; if there are others, it is communal, and all are blameworthy if they collude in refusing.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الحسن ، ومعناه أنه موكول إلى ديانتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author considers it plausible that literate people in the debtor’s locality owe a communal duty, made individual for whichever person the creditor selects to secure the debt.
rows.anchor: إنه واجب على الكفاية على من يعرف الكتابة من أهل مكان المتداينين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says a scribe is obliged to respond only when he is free.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما يجب على الكاتب في حال فراغه ، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, with a report from ʿAṭāʾ, regards the scribe’s duty as abrogated by the ban on harming a scribe or witness; the author objects that writing is not ordinarily harm except in rare cases such as great distance.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الضحاك ، وروي عن عطاء

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd say the rule was abrogated by the later permission to rely on mutual trust; the author says he will refute this.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي وابن جريج وابن زيد أنه منسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether a fee may be charged for writing depends on whether the service is obligatory: obligatory writing permits no fee, while a nonobligatory service may be paid.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الخلاف يختلف في جواز الأجر على الكتابة بين المتداينين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The documentation rule extends to all transactions for which parties seek written records and witnesses.
rows.anchor: ويلحق بالتداين جميع المعاملات التي يطلب فيها التوثق بالكتابة والإشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, as God taught him means writing in exact correspondence with divine instruction, not approximately; kāf is an adverbial cognate or describes an omitted verbal noun, and mā is relative.
rows.anchor: أي كتابة تشابه الذي علمه الله أن يكتبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s instruction is truth rooted in human nature: a scribe must record honestly without injustice or evasion, since people depart from truth through desire and alteration.
rows.anchor: أنه يكتب ما يعتقده ولا يجحف أو يوارب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The author connects the duty of truthful writing with the Prophet’s instruction to consult one’s own conscience even when people give contrary advice.
rows.anchor: وهذا يشير إليه قوله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, kāf conveys reciprocal recompense: the literate person repays God’s gift of literacy by using it to preserve others’ rights and avoiding deceit or omission.
rows.anchor: أي أن يكتب كتابة تكافىء تعليم الله إياه الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that alternative, kāf functions as an adverbial cognate or adjective of an understood object, mā is a verbal noun, and the phrase may attach to an yaktub.
rows.anchor: والكاف على هذا إما نائبة عن المفعول المطلق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows the phrase to attach instead to fal-yaktub; the author calls this a possible interpretive construction.
rows.anchor: وجوز صاحب ( الكشاف ) تعليقه بقوله فليكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fal-yaktub follows from the refusal prohibition, restates fa-uktubūhu, and reinforces both the command and the ban; it is repeated to link naturally to the command that the debtor dictate.
rows.anchor: وهو تصريح بمقتضى النهي وتكرير للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amalla is the Hijazi and Banū Asad form, while amlā is Tamīmī; the Qur’an uses both forms, and amalla is original with lām changed to yāʾ for ease.
rows.anchor: أمل وأملى لغتان : فالأولى لغة أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means conveying speech for someone to write, narrate, or memorize; restricting it to writing arose from focusing too narrowly on this verse, while al-Furqān confirms narration and memorization too.
rows.anchor: ليكتب عنه أو ليروى أو ليحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq here is the established due owed to the creditor.
rows.anchor: والحق هنا ما حق أي ثبت للدائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses must not insert conditions in a deed that the party did not dictate, unless the creditor delegated the details or showed the terms before contracting.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الأمر عبرة للشهود فإن منهم من يكتبون في شروط الحبس ونحوه ما لم يملله عليهم المشهود عليه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr takes both pronouns about fearing God and not reducing the amount to refer to the debtor, who must acknowledge the whole debt rather than shortchange the creditor.
rows.anchor: قاله سعيد بن جبير ، وهو على هذا أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the debtor as antecedent: the creditor is present and could object to omission, so the two pronouns more plausibly refer to the scribe, who might overlook dictated details.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن هذا بعيد إذ لا فائدة بهذه الوصاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safīh means cognitively impaired, ḍaʿīf means a minor, and one unable to dictate is incapacitated, such as someone simultaneously mute, blind, and deaf.
rows.anchor: والذي لا يستطيع أن يمل هو العاجز كمن به بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit pronoun in the phrase about inability prepares for the guardian’s command, showing disability does not remove the requirement to document what the person borrows.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتوهم الناس أن عجزه يسقط عنه واجب الإشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic and early Islamic practice a guardian could be a senior relative, father, trustee, or tribal notable; the Prophet told Hawāzin’s delegation to bring their ʿurafāʾ to present their case.
rows.anchor: وكان الأولياء قبل الإسلام وفي صدره كبراء القرابة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Hawāzin delegation report, the Prophet directs them to bring their tribal representatives to him, illustrating the early role of ʿurafāʾ in tribal affairs.
rows.anchor: قال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ليرفع إلي عرفاؤكم أمركم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardian’s declaration in the ward’s interest is valid when its basis is apparent; later jurists set it aside as a precaution against collusion that wastes vulnerable people’s property.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن إقرار الوصي والمقدم في حق المولى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to witness is additional to writing: writing preserves the contract’s wording and conditions against forgetfulness; jurists call it remembrance of the right and also a contract.
rows.anchor: وهو غيره وليس بيانا له إذ لو كان بيانا لما اقترن بالواو

rows.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza’s verse illustrates the written record as something preserved on parchment against later whims and injustice.
rows.anchor: قال الحارث بن حلزة : حذر الجور والتطاخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse gives pledge as the alternative when a writer cannot be found, without making unwritten testimony an intermediate option; thus a writer may also be one of the witnesses.
rows.anchor: فلم يجعل بين فقدان الكاتب وبين الرهن درجة وهي الشهادة بلا كتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names one scribe and two witnesses because people who are both literate and qualified to witness are uncommon.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل القرآن كاتبا وشاهدين لندرة الجمع بين معرفة الكتابة وأهلية الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istashhidū can mean simply have witnesses, with the s and t adding emphasis, or request two witnesses, making the creditor responsible for seeking testimony.
rows.anchor: فالسين والتاء فيه لمجرد التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creditor’s request is within a person’s capacity; the following ban on refusing then addresses the person asked to witness.
rows.anchor: تكليفا لمن يطلب منه صاحب الحق أن يشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahāda literally means presence and observation; here it means attending to observe a debt, while elsewhere it means testimony offered to establish a disputed claim, as in the four-witness rule.
rows.anchor: والشهادة حقيقتها الحضور والمشاهدة ، والمراد بها هنا

rows.speaker: جمهور السلف
rows.claim: The majority of early authorities interpret the command to obtain two witnesses as obligatory.
rows.anchor: قيل للوجوب ، وهو قول جمهور السلف

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The later majority of jurists, including Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad, regard witnessing as recommended; the discussion continues at the command to witness sales.
rows.anchor: قيل للندب ، وهو قول جمهور الفقهاء المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men among you means adult Muslim men: the address is to believers, minors lack judgment to assess the circumstances and suspicions, and the wording of rijāl itself excludes women and boys.
rows.anchor: أي من رجال المسلمين ، فحصل به شرطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues non-Muslims are excluded because religious difference prevents familiarity with one another’s integrity and duties; earlier religious communities did not clearly guarantee equal rights to outsiders.
rows.anchor: فكيف نعتد بشهادة هؤلاء الذين يرون المسلمين مارقين عن دين الحق مناوئين لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an alludes to non-Muslims’ asserted exemption from obligations toward the unlettered, as a reason not to rely on their testimony for Muslims.
rows.anchor: ليس علينا في الأميين سبيل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Khaybar killing report, the Prophet asked the Ansar for proof, then proposed that the Jews swear fifty oaths; the Ansar feared they would kill them and swear, so he paid the blood-money from charity funds.
rows.anchor: فانطلقوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فشكوا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes the report as confirming the Ansar’s claim that the Jews would not hesitate to kill them all and swear falsely.
rows.anchor: فقد أقر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قول الأنصار في اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two witnesses are the stipulated number for financial transactions.
rows.anchor: والعدد هو اثنان في المعاملات المالية كما هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition means that if two men are not present at the transaction, one man and two women may testify; the answer clause is elliptical, understood from the command to obtain witnesses.
rows.anchor: لم يحضر المعاملة رجلان بل حضر رجل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incomplete kāna avoids implying that women count only when two men are impossible, contrary to the majority; it also brings women into public affairs after their exclusion in pre-Islamic practice.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتوهم منه أن شهادة المرأتين لا تقبل إلا عند تعذر الرجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two women provide a safeguard against confusion or forgetting, which the author describes as more common among women by ordinary disposition; ḍalāl here means forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وهذه حيطة أخرى من تحريف الشهادة وهي خشية الاشتباه والنسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read an tadhilla with fatḥa, supplying a causal lām; the cause explains the pairing of women, and they read fa-tudhakkira in the subjunctive as coordinated with an tadhilla.
rows.anchor: قرأه الجمهور بفتح همزة أن على أنه محذوف منه لام التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads in tadhilla with kasra as a conditional, and raises tadhakkiru as the predicate of an omitted subject after fa; the author compares this syntax with Qur’an 5:95.
rows.anchor: على اعتبار إن شرطية وتضل فعل الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording appears to make forgetting the cause, the practical aim is preventing loss of the testimony; remembering is the consequence that completes the causal explanation.
rows.anchor: بل العلة هي ما يترتب على الضلال من إضاعة المشهود به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the wording as stressing reminder so strongly that the sentence names its enabling cause, comparing prepared timber to brace a leaning wall and weapons to repel an enemy.
rows.anchor: ووجهه صاحب ( الكشاف ) بأن فيه دلالة على الاهتمام

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib proposes that Arabic places the cause of a cause first and joins the actual cause with fa, a rule he presents as characteristic of the language.
rows.anchor: أن من شأن لغة العرب إذا ذكروا علة وكان للعلة علة قدموا ذكر علة العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a compound-cause account: the wording concisely expresses both avoiding loss when one woman forgets and gaining the benefit of the second woman’s reminder, better than al-Zamakhsharī’s account.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن مما ذكره صاحب ( الكشاف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating one of them instead of a pronoun lets either woman be subject or object without changing the meaning; an implicit pronoun would still have an unambiguous antecedent despite its different grammatical role.
rows.anchor: فلو أضمر للإحدى ضمير المفعول لكان المعاد واضحا سواء كان قوله إحداهما المظهر فاعلا أو مفعولا به

rows.speaker: التفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftāzānī notes that the repetition is not an ordinary replacement of a pronoun because the woman who reminds is not the forgetful one, and asks for the rhetorical reason.
rows.anchor: ومما ينبغي أن يتعرض له وجه تكرير لفظ إحداهما

rows.speaker: العصام
rows.claim: Al-ʿIṣām explains that the cause clause was fronted, preventing a pronoun and preventing the use of al-ukhrā before its counterpart had been named.
rows.anchor: فلما قدم إن ضلت وأبرز في معرض العلة لم يصح الإضمار

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafājī says the repetition conveys generality: either woman may forget or remind, so neither is merely a secondary reminder rather than a witness in her own right.
rows.anchor: النكتة الإبهام لأن كل واحدة من المرأتين يجوز عليها ما يجوز على صاحبتها

rows.speaker: شهاب الدين الغزنوي
rows.claim: Al-Ghaznawī answers al-Khafājī’s question in verse: because the statement could refer to either woman, a pronoun would wrongly identify one particular woman.
rows.anchor: تضل إحداهما فالقول محتمل كليهما فهي للإظهار مفتقره

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم المغربي
rows.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Maghribī reads the first one as one of the two testimonies and takes ḍalāl as loss through forgetting, then assigns the second one to a woman.
rows.anchor: إذ جعل إحداهما الأول مرادا به إحدى الشهادتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Maghribī’s interpretation as unsupported and contrived because it shifts the referents of the repeated expressions and scatters the pronouns.
rows.anchor: وهو تكلف وتشتيت للضمائر لا دليل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says repetition makes each clause stand alone like a maxim: forgetting explains why one woman is insufficient, and the second woman can keep the first woman’s testimony from failing altogether.
rows.anchor: قصد استقلال الجملة بمدلولها كيلا تحتاج إلى كلام آخر فيه معاد الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on refusing witnesses follows the command to the parties to seek them and ensures that the person asked will agree to attend.
rows.anchor: لما أمر المتعاقدين باستشهاد شاهدين نهى من يطلب إشهاده عن أن يأبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parties are commanded because they may neglect to secure witnesses, while witnesses are forbidden because they may refuse; each rule addresses the likely lapse and implies its opposite.
rows.anchor: فإن المتعاقدين يظن بهما إهمال الإشهاد فأمرا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invited are called witnesses in anticipation: their invitation itself signals that they are already committed to accept the witnessing role.
rows.anchor: وتسمية المدعوين شهداء باعتبار الأول القريبب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān, and a report from Ibn ʿAbbās understand the omitted object as being called to bear witness at the transaction; refusing to bear it is forbidden all the more.
rows.anchor: أي إذا ما دعوا إلى الشهادة أي التحمل ، وهذا قول قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, understands the invitation to include both bearing witness and later giving testimony.
rows.anchor: والأداء معا ؛ قاله الحسن ، وابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid limits the invitation to giving testimony; the author notes his rationale that invitees are not truly witnesses until they have borne witness, but considers it weakened by the next verse’s ban on concealing testimony.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : إذا ما دعوا إلى الأداء خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes the omitted object broadly: people may be called both to witness the transaction and to give testimony when proof is later needed.
rows.anchor: لإفادة شمول ما يدعون لأجله في التعاقد

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib says bearing witness is a communal duty when needed, while giving testimony from a distance of two barīd is an individual duty and cannot be replaced by an oath.
rows.anchor: والتحمل حيث يفتقر إليه فرض كفاية والأداء من نحو البريدين إن كانا اثنين فرض عين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The author applies the earlier disagreement about scribes: accepting the request to bear witness becomes individual when designated, and giving testimony is individually obligatory if it causes no bodily or financial harm; Abū Ḥanīfa makes performance communal unless uniquely required, subject to court integrity, proximity, admissibility, and a claimant’s request.
rows.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة الأداء فرض كفاية إلا إذا تعين عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects to making testimony depend on each witness’s own varying judgments about these conditions, calling that a door to excessive legal qualification.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه التعليقات رد بالشهادة إلى مختلف اجتهادات الشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small and large debts represent trivial and substantial amounts; since small transactions are more frequent, parties are told not to tire of recording them.
rows.anchor: تعميم في أكوان أو أحوال الديون المأمور بكتابتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address primarily concerns contracting parties and by implication includes the scribe, who must write when they request it.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للمتداينين أصالة ، ويستتبع ذلك خطاب الكاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition concerns the result of weariness—leaving the debt unwritten—because involuntary boredom itself cannot be prohibited.
rows.anchor: لأن السآمة تحصل للنفس من غير اختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes sāmah as a figurative expression for laziness and laxity.
rows.anchor: وقيل السآمة هنا كناية عن الكسل والتهاون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaghīran aw kabīran is parsed either as a circumstantial accusative describing the debt or as a phrase with kāna and its subject omitted.
rows.anchor: وانتصب صغيرا أو كبيرا على الحال من الضمير المنصوب بتكتبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Small precedes large, unlike the expected order, to emphasize complete coverage, since small debts are more frequent and might be neglected, while mentioning only small debts could imply large ones need no writing.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الصغير على الكبير هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilā ajalihi is circumstantial: the record must specify the debt up to the agreed term.
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير المنصوب بتكتبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is more just because it better preserves the right, supports giving testimony, and reduces doubt; these three reasons make evidence clear and free of suspicion.
rows.anchor: أقوم للشهادة ، أي أعون على إقامتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to the preceding documentation rules collectively, and the verse supports grounding one legal ruling in several reasons.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة عائد إلى جميع ما تقدم باعتبار أنه مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqsatu derives from the quadriliteral aqsaṭa, meaning to act justly, not from qaṣaṭa, meaning to act unjustly; aqwamu derives from aqāma al-shahāda.
rows.anchor: من أقسط بمعنى عدل ، وهو رباعي

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Sībawayh permits comparative forms from hamzated quadriliteral verbs, whether the hamza makes a verb transitive or not; al-Zamakhsharī alternatively analyzes aqsatu as a nisba form.
rows.anchor: جار على قول سيبويه بجواز صوغ التفضيل والتعجب من الرباعي المهموز

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives aqsatu from qāsiṭ, meaning possessing a share of justice; the author finds the pattern and derivation from a noun problematic.
rows.anchor: وجوز صاحب ( الكشاف ) أن يكون أقسط مشتقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that a nisba from a verbal noun resembles a derivative because the verbal noun is the origin of derivation, and suggests aqwamu may also come from qawuma and yield the adjective qawīm.
rows.anchor: والجواب عندي أن النسب هنا لما كان إلى المصدر شابه المشتق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate-trade exception qualifies the general range of transactions; it may be a disconnected exception because an immediate cash sale is not a debt.
rows.anchor: لأن التجارة الحاضرة ليست من الدين في شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāḍirah means immediate, without delay; ḥāḍir, ʿājil, and nājiz are synonyms, as are debt, term, and deferred payment.
rows.anchor: والحاضرة الناجزة ، التي لا تأخير فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tudīrūnahā baynakum explains the immediate trade and likely indicates why writing is dispensable: the parties’ exchange itself makes the transaction evident.
rows.anchor: ولعل فائدة ذكره الإيماء إلى تعليل الرخصة في ترك الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats tudīrūnahā as an explanation of trade, like the poet’s explanation of two needs by asking how they can meet; it may also be a second descriptive phrase.
rows.anchor: جعل صاحب ( الكشاف ) كيف يلتقيان بيانا لحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connected-exception reading takes immediate trade to mean a debt due soon and exempts that debt from writing, but the author considers this remote.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالتجارة الحاضرة المؤجلة إلى أجل قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit statement that there is no blame restates the exception and signals a concession; writing nevertheless remains preferable.
rows.anchor: من الإشارة إلى أن هذا الحكم رخصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers vocalize tijāratun as nominative with kāna complete; ʿĀṣim reads it accusative with kāna incomplete and an understood noun repeated as predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تجارة بالرفع : على أن تكون تامة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Sībawayh cites ʿAmr ibn Shās’s verse with an implied repeated subject and predicate as a parallel for the incomplete-kāna reading.
rows.anchor: كما في قول عمرو بن شاس أنشده سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written form allā is contracted from an lā.
rows.anchor: أصله أن لا فرسم مدغما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses are also required for a sale without debt when it is not ordinary immediate commerce, completing the categories of debt, credit sales, immediate trade, and immediate noncommercial sales.
rows.anchor: تشريع للإشهاد عند البيع ولو بغير دين إذا كان البيع غير تجارة حاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the command as only referring to immediate trade and retaining witnesses without writing is very unlikely, since writing was instituted to support witnessing and documentation.
rows.anchor: لأن الكتابة ما شرعت إلا لأجل الإشهاد والتوثق

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Saʿīd, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn Jurayj, al-Nakhaʿī, Jābir ibn Zayd, Dāwūd, and al-Ṭabarī take witnessing at sales as obligatory.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي موسى الأشعري

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet had a sale witnessed and wrote a document for al-ʿAdāʾ ibn Khālid describing the purchased slave as free of defects and prohibited liabilities.
rows.anchor: وقد أشهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على بيع عبد باعه للعداء بن خالد بن هوذة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī, followed by Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad, regard witnessing as recommended; they cite the Prophet’s sales without witnesses.
rows.anchor: وهو قول مالك ، وأبي حنيفة ، والشافعي ، وأحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers the argument from unwitnessed sales by limiting those cases to contexts of mutual trust and refers to the following trust provision; he also rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s earlier rationale.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك في مواضع الائتمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yaḍārr can be active or passive, allowing the ban to cover either scribes and witnesses harming the parties or the parties harming them; the wording deliberately carries both compatible rules.
rows.anchor: لأن يضار يحتمل البناء للمعلوم وللمجهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm includes parties burdening a scribe or witness with hardship, loss, or exposure to punishment, and witnesses causing a party to lose a right or suffer the burden of answering.
rows.anchor: إدخال الضر بأن يوقع المتعاقدان الشاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse grounds procedural protections: avoid distant travel and destabilizing questioning after long delays; public funds should cover witnesses’ travel, lodging, and resulting family losses to support justice.
rows.anchor: أنه ينبغي لولاة الأمور جعل جانب من مال بيت المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of do refers to causing the prohibited harm; fusūq means grave sin, as in the denunciation of the term after faith.
rows.anchor: حذف مفعول تفعلوا وهو معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God presents piety as the basis of good conduct and abstention from wrongdoing; the teaching clause recalls Islam’s gift of knowledge of law and the order of life, and its present tense suggests its continuance.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتقوى لأنها ملاك الخير ، وبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the conjunction in wayuʿallimukumu Allāh causally, as meaning that God teaches because of piety; the author rejects treating this as a special grammatical meaning of wāw.
rows.anchor: إن الواو فيه للتعليل أي ليعلمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the divine name across three clauses gives each independent force, so hearing one without another still conveys its point; it also creates awe.
rows.anchor: لقصد التنويه بكل جملة منها حتى تكون مستقلة الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem in al-Ḥamāsa repeats al-luʾm in three lines to censure a tribe and its descendants, illustrating deliberate repetition; al-Jurjānī says taste can discern rhetorical effects that resist explanation.
rows.anchor: قول الحماسي : اللؤم أكرم من وبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing and testimony rules apply in ordinary settled conditions when available; when travel prevents finding someone to write or witness, a pledge supplies the final transactional arrangement, extended to similar circumstances.
rows.anchor: فجميع ما تقدم حكم في الحضر والمكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rihān is a plural of rahn, also pluralized as ruhan; the majority of the ten readers vocalize it with kasra then fatḥa, while Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr use ḍamma on both letters.
rows.anchor: والرهان جمع رهن ويجمع أيضا على رهن بضم الراء وضم الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahn names the pledged object by its verbal noun; the debtor places property in the creditor’s possession as security, and the root means detention, as in the verse about every soul held by its deeds.
rows.anchor: والرهن هنا اسم للشيء المرهون تسمية للمفعول بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line uses a pledge that cannot be released as an image of a debt secured by property held until payment.
rows.anchor: قال زهير : وفارقتك برهن لا فكاك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs commonly pledged property for guarantees and blood-money, sometimes even sons or prominent men as hostages.
rows.anchor: فقد كانوا يرهنون في الحمالات والديات إلى أن يقع دفعها

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s poem recalls Kisrā seeking children as hostages, which the speaker vowed not to provide lest they be corrupted.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى يذكر أن كسرى رام أخذ رهائن من أبنائهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن همام السلولي
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hammām al-Sulūlī’s verse describes escaping danger while leaving Mālik as a hostage.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن همام السلولي : فلما خشيت

rows.speaker: كعب بن الأشرف
rows.claim: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf asked ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf to pledge his sons as hostages.
rows.anchor: ومن حديث كعب بن الأشرفف أنه قال لعبد الرحمن بن عوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the parties trust one another, the creditor is the one trusting and the debtor is the one trusted with the creditor’s property or right.
rows.anchor: أي إن أمن كل من المتداينين الآخر أي وثق بعضكم بأمانة بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amāna derives from giving security; it can name the trusted property itself, and its possessive construction resembles a verbal noun joined to its object.
rows.anchor: والأمانة مصدر آمنه إذا جعله آمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a debt or pledge an amāna gives the right gravity: failing to return it is betrayal, and a Prophetic report commands returning deposits without reciprocating betrayal.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : أد الأمانة إلى من ائتمنك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet commands returning a trust to its owner and not betraying someone even if that person betrayed you.
rows.anchor: أد الأمانة إلى من ائتمنك ولا تخن من خانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Performance means payment or fulfillment, return of the thing itself or its equivalent when fungible, and not denying the debt, as in the command to return trusts to their owners.
rows.anchor: ورد الشيء أو رد مثله فيما لا تقصد أعيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the majority who treat debt documentation as recommended, this trust provision completes the guidance: parties may document and witness, or rely on their known honesty.
rows.anchor: تعتبر تكميلا لطلب الكتابة والإشهاد طلب ندب واستحباب عند الذين حملوا الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust clause is followed by a charge to both parties to fulfill what they owe and fear God.
rows.anchor: وأتبع هذا البيان بوصاية كلا المتعاملين بأن يؤديا الأمانة ويتقيا الله

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Jurayj, Jābir ibn Zayd, al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān, and an attribution to Abū Saʿīd say mutual trust abrogated the earlier duty to write and witness debts.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الشعبي ، وابن جريج ، وجابر بن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abū Saʿīd’s position is sound, the author says their term abrogation uses an older sense meaning specification of general circumstances or times.
rows.anchor: ومحمل قولهم وقولل أبي سعيد إن صح ذلك عنه

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Those who retain obligatory writing and testimony, including al-Ṭabarī, confine the trust clause to the travel-pledge case; the author says al-Ṭabarī’s explanation is unclear.
rows.anchor: كما صرح به الطبري ولم يأت بكلام واضح في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests this narrow view could mean that travelers lacking a pledge may proceed only if they trust each other, though its adherents do not clearly state this and may omit it to encourage mutual generosity.
rows.anchor: إن هذه الآية تعني حالة تعذر وجود الرهن في حالة السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers an independent rule covering every debt setting and transaction: testimony, pledge, repayment, and sale; the undefined baʿḍ includes trust from either direction.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية تشريع مستقل يعم جميع الأحوال المتعلقة بالديون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A creditor trusts a debtor by dispensing with witnesses and a pledge; a debtor trusts a creditor by giving a pledge worth more than the debt, so each must honor the other’s entrusted right.
rows.anchor: فرب الدين يأتمن المدين إذا لم ير حاجة إلى الإشهاد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor must repay without delay or denial; the creditor holding an overvalued pledge must return it without denial or withholding any part, since the collateral exceeds the debt.
rows.anchor: فأداء المدين أمانته بدفع الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amāna refers both to the quality of being trustworthy and to the entrusted object.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الأمانة مستعمل في معنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects pre-Islamic foreclosure, by which the creditor became owner of a pledge after nonpayment at the deadline; the Prophet forbade a pledge from being closed off in this way.
rows.anchor: فيؤخذ من هذا التفسير إبطال غلق الرهن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that a pledge is not forfeited to the creditor.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لا يغلق الرهن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s verse reflects the old practice of a pledge becoming locked and irredeemable.
rows.anchor: قال زهير : وفارقتك برهنن لا فكاك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual trust means both parties say they need no witnesses because each trusts the other; this avoids reviving suspicion between debtors and creditors.
rows.anchor: أن يقول كلا المتعاملين للآخر : لا حاجة لنا بالإشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating God’s name before the command to fear Him adds solemn awe even though a pronoun could have been used.
rows.anchor: وذكر اسم الجلالة فيه مع إمكان الاستغناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority retain the hamza in alladhī ʾūtumina after the connecting hamza drops, since there is then no reason to change it into a long vowel.
rows.anchor: فقرأه الجمهور بكسر ذال الذي وبهمزة ساكنة بعد كسرة الذال

rows.speaker: ورش
rows.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Jaʿfar read al-ladhītumina, changing the hamza to wāw under the passive-form vowel and then wāw to yāʾ after the connecting hamza drops.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ورش عن نافع ، وأبو عمرو ، وأبو جعفر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads alladhī awtumin, using wāw to represent the hamza following a ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These recitational differences concern oral delivery and do not conflict with the written consonantal text.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف راجع إلى وجه الأداء فلا مخالفة فيه لرسم المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general ban on concealing testimony is a second charge to witnesses, summarizing the commands to write justly and not refuse testimony.
rows.anchor: وصاية ثانية للشهداء تجمع الشهادات في جميع الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prohibition repeats whenever the occasion to commit the act arises; witnesses should disclose what they know whenever needed and may act earlier if absence, forgetfulness, or death could erase the evidence.
rows.anchor: فلذلك كان حقا على من تحمل شهادة بحق ألا يكتمه عند عروض إعلانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier commands to make testimony clear and to accept an invitation show the law’s concern to reveal rights, not suppress them.
rows.anchor: وأنه حرض الشاهد على الحضور للإشهاد إذا طلب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the best witnesses those who bring their testimony before being asked; Mālik records it, and Muslim and the four Sunan collections transmit it from him.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ألا أخبركم بخير الشهداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this interpretation is supported by both transmitted evidence and reasoning.
rows.anchor: فهذا وجه تفسير الآية تظاهر فيه الأثر والنظر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a sound report from Abū Hurayra, the Prophet praises the earliest generations and then warns of later people who testify before being asked.
rows.anchor: ثم يخلف قوم يشهدون قبل أن يستشهدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the concealer’s heart sinful attributes the act to the mental faculty that intends it; the heart signifies perception, emotion, and intention, which causes the committed sin.
rows.anchor: والقلب اسم للإدراك والانفعالات النفسية والنوايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about concealing testimony threatens punishment: because only ignorance could prevent a capable God from requiting action, divine knowledge implies judgment.
rows.anchor: كناية عن المجازاة بمثل الصنيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God owns everything in heaven and earth supports the preceding assertion of His knowledge and judgment; the following clause about inner thoughts is the explicit proof and focus.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان ذلك تعريضا بالوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership is the inferential premise: He is the servants’ Lord, so no deed or its recompense escapes Him; the clause about exposed or hidden thoughts is conjoined to it.
rows.anchor: فلا يفوته عملكم والجزاء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah closes by renewing believers’ resolve and readiness against the enemy so the defeat they suffered will not demoralize them.
rows.anchor: ختمت السورة بوصاية جامعة للمؤمنين تجدد عزيمتهم وتبعث الهمم إلى دوام الاستعداد للعدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience gathers the virtues; mutual perseverance means holding firm against another patient opponent, a harder and more precarious trial because the rival may equal or surpass one.
rows.anchor: وهي الصبر في وجه الصابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A contest is won by whoever endures longer; if one yields before the other tires, one gains nothing from patience.
rows.anchor: لأن نتيجة الصبر تكون لأطول الصابرين صبرا

rows.speaker: زفر بن الحارث
rows.claim: Zufar ibn al-Ḥārith’s verse excuses a retreat by saying both sides drank the same cup, but the enemy proved more patient in facing death.
rows.anchor: كما قال زفر بن الحارث في اعتذاره عن الانهزام

rows.speaker: شاعر العرب الذي لم يعرف اسمه
rows.claim: An unnamed Arab poet says perseverance in battle brings fire upon one’s enemies, illustrating the author’s claim that mutual endurance wins war.
rows.anchor: كما قال شاعر العرب الذي لم يعرف اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribāṭ means keeping horses tethered for watch at vulnerable approaches beyond active fighting, so Muslims remain alert to surprise attacks after Uḥud; the Confederates later attacked in just such circumstances.
rows.anchor: وهي مفاعلة من الربط ، وهو ربط الخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribāṭ was already a pre-Islamic practice of guarding tribal approaches and mountain passes; after Islamic expansion it included land and coastal frontier stations vulnerable to enemy landings.
rows.anchor: وكانت المرابطة معروفة في الجاهلية وهي ربط الفرس للحراسة في الثغور

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd’s poem vividly depicts a mounted guard watching the tribal settlement from a high lookout until darkness covers the vulnerable passes.
rows.anchor: وما رأيت من وصف ذلك مثل لبيد في معلقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands frontier guard just as He commands fighting, in the established sense of maintaining watch at land and sea approaches.
rows.anchor: فأمر الله بالرباط كما أمر بالجهاد بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators instead take ribāṭ as preparing horses tethered for battle and argue there were no frontier campaigns in the Prophet’s time; the author says this misses the established meaning.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : أراد بقوله

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is associated with interpreting ribāṭ as waiting for one prayer after another, based on Abū Hurayra’s report in Mālik’s Muwaṭṭaʾ.
rows.anchor: ونسب هذا لأبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet described waiting for the next prayer after one as ribāṭ, repeating the phrase three times.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says prayer-waiting is metaphorical, like the reports that strength is not merely wrestling and poverty is not merely asking for food; he also invokes the saying about returning from lesser to greater struggle as figurative.
rows.anchor: والحق أن معنى هذا الحديث على التشبيه
